tagline: Past the state's first town, out through drained swamp and refuge.
intro: The byway leaves the waterfront at Washington, the first town named for George Washington, and follows the Pamlico River east to Bath and Belhaven. Past Scranton, drainage canals and trees close in on both sides for seven miles. Then US 264 runs out across Hyde County past Swan Quarter, Lake Mattamuskeet and Engelhard, and through the Alligator River refuge to Manns Harbor.

Much of the farmland was swamp until it was drained in the early 20th century. At Mattamuskeet, between 1911 and 1934, investors built the world's largest pumping plant to drain the whole lake and laid out a town called New Holland on its bed. In 1934 the government bought it for a migratory bird refuge.

moments.title: Bath
moments.text: North Carolina's first town, chartered in 1705, where Blackbeard settled on a royal pardon in 1718 and was back at piracy within the year.

moments.title: Lake Mattamuskeet
moments.text: The state's largest natural lake averages two or three feet deep and is a major wintering ground for pintails, teal, Canada geese and tundra swans.

moments.title: Alligator River National Wildlife Refuge
moments.text: The last stretch crosses a refuge kept for endangered red wolves, alligators and red-cockaded woodpeckers, which also holds the Dare County Bombing Range.

practical: Engelhard is the last stop for fuel or restrooms for about 40 miles, until Manns Harbor.
